caption_en: Novi Zagreb is the part of the city south of the Sava. Building there began in the 1950s, under mayor Većeslav Holjevac.
caption_sv: Novi Zagreb dio je grada južno od Save. Gradnja je ondje počela 1950-ih, za gradonačelnika Većeslava Holjevca.

caption_en: The Bridge of Freedom, by Krunoslav Tonković, opened on 2 September 1959. It carries the avenue that now bears Holjevac's name.
caption_sv: Most slobode, djelo Krunoslava Tonkovića, otvoren je 2. rujna 1959. Njime prolazi avenija koja danas nosi Holjevčevo ime.
photo_caption_en: The Bridge of Freedom from the northern embankment

caption_en: Holjevac moved the Zagreb Fair to the meadows across the river. The City's register dates the fair grounds 1955 to 1964.
caption_sv: Holjevac je Zagrebački velesajam preselio na livade preko Save. Gradski registar datira velesajam od 1955. do 1964.
photo_caption_en: A concrete shell sculpture in the fair grounds
photo_caption_sv: Betonska ljuska, skulptura na prostoru Velesajma

caption_en: In Siget, Super Andrija by Miroslav Cantinelli was built in 1973. It has 14 floors and 488 flats.
caption_sv: U Sigetu je 1973. izgrađen Super Andrija, djelo Miroslava Cantinellija. Ima 14 katova i 488 stanova.

caption_en: Mamutica in Travno followed in 1974. It is about 240 metres long and 60 metres high, and about 5,000 people live in it.
caption_sv: Mamutica u Travnom slijedila je 1974. Duga je oko 240 metara, visoka 60 metara, a u njoj živi oko 5000 ljudi.

caption_en: The Museum of Contemporary Art moved here, into a new building by Igor Franić. It opened on 11 December 2009.
caption_sv: Muzej suvremene umjetnosti preselio je ovamo, u novu zgradu Igora Franića. Otvorena je 11. prosinca 2009.
sources: Museum of Contemporary Art; landmark card

caption_en: Most buildings south of the Sava have no year on this map yet, so they appear only when the timeline reaches today.
caption_sv: Većina zgrada južno od Save na ovoj karti još nema godinu, pa se pojavljuju tek kad vremenska crta dođe do danas.
